overview.reason: Establish a concise, communication-focused account of the project before technical probing.
overview.prompt: Give a concise interview-style introduction to the project, targeting about 1–2 minutes as a communication target rather than a stopwatch test. Explain its purpose, the version-token freshness approach, your design contribution, the agent-assisted implementation boundary, and the outcome or known limits. Do not focus on labels, dates, exact numbers, or original wording.
overview.recall_reminder: Use the supplied project context. This tests synthesis, not recall of labels, dates, exact numbers, or source wording.
evaluation_criteria: Explains the version-token freshness approach accurately.
Distinguishes the user's design contribution from the agent-assisted implementation.
States the known outcome or limits without inventing production operation or repeated-context responsibility.
Uses a clear, structured interview-style explanation.

areas.unverified_capability: Reason about the freshness contract created by version tokens within the user's design responsibility.
areas.demanding_prompt: Explain why rejecting a cache entry when its version token changes preserves the freshness contract, and identify the design boundary this rule establishes.
areas.intermediate_prompt: Using one concrete token-change scenario, explain why the cached entry must be rejected.
areas.simple_prompt: State the condition that makes a cached entry stale in this design.
areas.immediately_higher_capability: Analyze a token-transition edge case and defend whether the contract remains correct under that condition, with a precise rationale.

hard: Explains the causal link between token change and rejection.
Identifies the freshness property protected by the contract.
Keeps the reasoning within the user's design role and distinguishes design from implementation.
intermediate: Correctly predicts rejection of the affected entry.
Connects the prediction to freshness rather than to an unrelated cache behavior.
simple: States that a token mismatch makes the entry stale.

areas.unverified_capability: Adapt the version-token freshness design to a similar problem when token reads may be stale.
areas.demanding_prompt: The token source is eventually consistent, so a lookup can read an older token after the token has changed. Adapt the freshness contract to reduce false acceptance of stale entries, and explain the key limitation of your adaptation.
areas.intermediate_prompt: Under the eventually consistent token-source condition, propose one change to the lookup contract that prevents a known stale-entry acceptance case.
areas.simple_prompt: Under this condition, identify why comparing the cached token with one possibly stale token read may accept an outdated entry.
areas.immediately_higher_capability: Design and justify a verification strategy that distinguishes genuine freshness from stale token-source observations under eventual consistency.

hard: Identifies the failure mode caused by stale token reads.
Proposes a coherent contract adaptation tied to that failure mode.
States a concrete limitation or residual uncertainty without claiming the adaptation was implemented.
intermediate: Names one specific stale-entry acceptance case.
Proposes one relevant contract change that addresses that case.
Keeps the proposal within the version-token mechanism.
simple: Explains why a stale token read can make an outdated entry appear valid.
Does not claim that the proposed adaptation was actually deployed.

areas.changed_condition: The token source is eventually consistent, so a lookup can read an older token after the token has changed.

model_drift_limitation.reason: Alias identity can drift; each raw response and exact configuration are retained.
